title: Ashwin Says Dropping Kuldeep Against West Indies Lacked Common Sense
excerpt: The former India spinner argued Kuldeep's googly troubles West Indies batters and could have saved 15-20 runs in Hyderabad, where India lost by 24 to level the series 2-2.
body:
• Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin said leaving Kuldeep Yadav out of the fourth T20I against West Indies in Hyderabad lacked common sense.
  • West Indies made 247/3, with Shai Hope unbeaten on 102 off 50 balls, and beat India by 24 runs to level the five-match series 2-2.
  • Kuldeep took 2/33 in Lucknow and 1/53 in Ranchi before being left out in Indore and Hyderabad; against West Indies in T20Is he has 20 wickets in 11 matches at 15.70.
  • The series decider is in Bengaluru on October 17 — watch whether India restore their wrist-spinner on a ground where bounce is expected.

Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has criticised the team management for leaving Kuldeep Yadav out of the fourth T20I against West Indies in Hyderabad on October 14, saying the decision lacked common sense against batters who struggle to read the wrist-spinner. Ashwin made the remarks on his YouTube channel, Ash Ki Baat, according to Sportskeeda and CricTracker.

The cost of the call was visible on the scoreboard. West Indies posted 247/3 in 20 overs, powered by Shai Hope's unbeaten 102 off 50 balls, and India were bowled out for 223 in 19.3 overs to lose by 24 runs. The result levelled the five-match series 2-2 ahead of the decider in Bengaluru on October 17.

"If you are leaving Kuldeep out against them, it lacks a bit of common sense."

— Ravichandran Ashwin, on his YouTube channel Ash Ki Baat

Ashwin's Argument, in Detail

Ashwin's point was matchup-specific. Hyderabad, he argued, is a ground where a spinner can expect some bounce, and West Indies batters have struggled to pick Kuldeep's googly and leg-spin. On that combination, he estimated Kuldeep's presence could have made a difference of 15 to 20 runs — roughly the margin of defeat.

https://x.com/cricketnext/status/2110684282314473761

The record supports the matchup claim. Sportskeeda noted Kuldeep has taken 20 wickets in 11 T20Is against West Indies at an average of 15.70 and an economy rate of 7.13, with best figures of 3/12. In all T20Is he has 98 wickets in 56 matches at 14.20. CricTracker added that Kuldeep had also taken seven wickets in the preceding ODI series, which India won 2-1.

Indore Was Different, Ranchi Was Not Kuldeep's Fault

Ashwin was not criticising every omission. He said he would still endorse leaving Kuldeep out in Indore, where the ground is small and hard on spinners. Captain Shreyas Iyer had explained that call by the need for a yorker-bowling option on a small, batting-friendly ground, with pacer Prince Yadav brought in, CricTracker reported.

What Ashwin rejected was the implied narrative after Ranchi. Kuldeep took 1/53 there as India failed to defend 249, and Ashwin argued that making an issue of that performance — effectively blaming the spinner for a collective failure to defend a huge total — was wrong in itself. His objection, in other words, was to a knee-jerk reaction becoming a selection policy for the next two matches.

What Happens Next

India now go to Bengaluru for the October 17 decider with the series level and their bowling combination under public scrutiny from one of the game's most respected spin minds. Restoring Kuldeep would be the direct answer to Ashwin's critique; leaving him out again would require the seam attack to prove, on the night, that Hyderabad was about execution rather than selection.

For diaspora fans following the series, the debate is familiar and concrete: in T20 cricket, a proven matchup is an asset you spend carefully. Ashwin's verdict is that India left theirs unused — twice — and paid for it in Hyderabad.
